findings.claim: Students must be able to define and apply all five.
findings.truth: AQA GCSE Drama does not prescribe Stanislavski or a required list of his techniques. Naturalism is an example of a performance style, so these techniques are optional tools rather than five required items.
findings.evidence: AQA GCSE Drama 8261 specification, 3.2 and 4.2; AQA 2023 Component 2 examiner report: no mandatory requirement to use a practitioner.

findings.claim: Artaud even proposed spaces without fixed seats, where the audience moves through the action as it unfolds around them.
findings.truth: Artaud's first Theatre of Cruelty manifesto places the audience centrally on mobile chairs while the action occurs around them. This is surround staging, not standard promenade staging (where the audience travels) or theatre in the round (where the audience surrounds a central stage). Recommended option: replace the linked promenade and in-the-round teaching with the source-faithful central-audience formulation throughout the lesson.
findings.evidence: Artaud, The Theatre and Its Double (1958), pp. 96-97, reproduced in fetched academic sources; the passage specifies mobile chairs in the middle of the room and spectacle all around them.
findings.ruling: Central-audience surround staging per the first manifesto.

findings.claim: Frantic Assembly was founded in 1994 by Scott Graham and Steven Hoggett.
findings.truth: Frantic Assembly was founded in 1994 by Scott Graham, Steven Hoggett and Vicki Middleton.
findings.evidence: Frantic Assembly, History; OCR Topic Exploration Pack written by Scott Graham and Frantic Assembly, p. 2.

findings.claim: The founder flashcard names only Scott Graham and Steven Hoggett.
findings.truth: The flashcard must also name co-founder Vicki Middleton.
findings.evidence: Frantic Assembly, History; OCR Topic Exploration Pack written by Scott Graham and Frantic Assembly, p. 2.

findings.claim: Complicite was founded by Simon McBurney in 1983.
findings.truth: Complicite was founded in 1983 by Annabel Arden, Fiona Gordon, Marcello Magni and Simon McBurney.

findings.claim: The four most relevant for GCSE Drama are Frantic Assembly, Complicite, DV8 and Steven Berkoff.
findings.truth: AQA does not mandate named practitioners. Frantic Assembly, Complicite and DV8 are companies; Steven Berkoff is a practitioner. They can be presented as useful examples, not as the four prescribed GCSE choices.
findings.evidence: AQA GCSE Drama 8261 specification, subject content; AQA 2023 Component 2 examiner report: no mandatory requirement to use a practitioner; Complicite and DV8 official histories.

findings.claim: Frantic Assembly's signature movement devising method is called round-by-through-under.
findings.truth: The fetched Frantic/OCR material confirms the Frantic Method and Chair Duets but does not verify this term. Secondary teaching material instead uses 'round-by-through'. Recommended option: verify the preferred term directly with Frantic Assembly, then update every repeated use and answer option consistently if 'round-by-through' is confirmed.
findings.evidence: OCR Topic Exploration Pack created by Scott Graham and Frantic Assembly, pp. 1-4; no fetched primary source verified 'round-by-through-under'.
findings.ruling: Frantic Assembly's term is round/by/through; the extra 'under' removed everywhere in L4.

summary: Four lessons were checked. Five verified surgical corrections are supplied; two cross-field terminology and staging issues need adjudication before coordinated edits.
